SCAPULA_3DCT_NOTCH_2022.citation: An anatomical study for the location of suprascapular and spinoglenoid notches using three-dimensional computed tomography images of scapula.
SCAPULA_3DCT_NOTCH_2022.use: Landmark-compatible 3D scapular constraints, especially AA/TS-like transverse geometry.
SCAPULA_3DCT_NOTCH_2022.caveat: Older Far East Asian clinical sample; some distances correlate with height. Use exact landmark mapping and additional sources before freezing final dimensions.

measurement_semantics.d1: supraglenoid tubercle to infraglenoid tubercle; not superior/inferior articular rim extents
measurement_semantics.d2: maximum transverse glenoid span perpendicular to the tubercle d1 line; not automatically anterior/posterior rim landmark chord
measurement_semantics.d3: posterolateral acromion to medial scapular-spine-border midpoint, direct 3D landmark distance
measurement_semantics.d4: superior angle to inferior angle, direct 3D landmark distance
measurement_semantics.d5: perpendicular spinoglenoid-notch offset from the AA-to-medial-spine reference line
measurement_semantics.d6: AA to projection foot of spinoglenoid notch on AA-to-medial-spine line, not direct AA-to-notch chord
measurement_semantics.d7: AA to projection foot of suprascapular notch on AA-to-medial-spine line, not direct AA-to-notch chord
measurement_semantics.d8: lateral acromial border to projection foot associated with its perpendicular bisector, not an arbitrary direct LA-to-notch chord

SCAPULA_3DCT_NOTCH_2022.audit_correction_20261008: Full-text methods/figure captions resolve d6/d7 as projected line distances and d1 as tubercle distance. Legacy short measurement keys are retained for provenance but do not define direct chords.

SCAPULA_AC_LATERAL_2026.citation: Kang N, Brassett C. Scapular morphometrics inform anatomic landmark distances for arthroscopic suprascapular nerve decompression: a cadaveric study. JSES Int. 2026.
SCAPULA_AC_LATERAL_2026.sample: 20 cadaveric shoulders from 10 White British donors; 5 male, 5 female; mean age 80.8 ± 8.9 y
SCAPULA_AC_LATERAL_2026.measurement_definition: Direct distance from the posterior aspect of the AC joint to the lateral acromion, measured in the line of the posterior clavicle/acromion. The full text explicitly reports this direct result; it is not obtained by subtracting STSL distances.
SCAPULA_AC_LATERAL_2026.use: Direct transverse/lateral AC-to-lateral-acromion constraint for the canonical shoulder scaffold; also independent scapular size cross-check.
SCAPULA_AC_LATERAL_2026.caveat: Small, old cadaver sample and mixed sex. Use as a direct landmark relation with uncertainty, not as a sole final target. Preserve the distinction from the earlier invalid inference that subtracted two independently measured STSL distances.

LEE_2024_SCAPULA_RAW_3D.citation: Lee ECS, Lawrence RL, Rainbow MJ. Sexual dimorphism and allometry in human scapula shape. Journal of Anatomy (2024).

landmark_mapping_1based.5: intersection of spine with vertebral border; medial spine landmark
landmark_mapping_1based.14: root of spine; distinct from medial-border point 5
landmark_mapping_1based.19: shallowest glenoid midline point, not GH sphere centre

LEE_2024_SCAPULA_RAW_3D.use: Provisional rigidly aligned relative 29-landmark envelope and direct stature regression; no absolute joint centres.
limitations: Independent endpoint-matched confirmation required before exact freeze.
2022 d1 is tubercle-to-tubercle, not this dataset glenoid-rim chord.
Exterior and interior acromial angles must not be substituted to force agreement.
Sparse measured landmarks are evidence, not a complete production bone surface.
